intent: Practise one-to-one correspondence when counting up to 8 objects, tracking counted items to ensure each is counted once without skips or double-counts.

data.title: Count the Fish!
data.description: Practise one-to-one correspondence by counting friendly fish one by one up to eight.

challenges.instruction: Can you count all the fish? Tap each one!
challenges.hint: Try tapping them slowly one by one from left to right.
challenges.narration: Let us count these friendly fish together in a straight line.

challenges.instruction: Let us count a few more fish. Touch each one as we go!
challenges.hint: Remember to touch every single fish once without skipping any.
challenges.narration: Here are some more fish swimming in a row. Can you count them?

challenges.instruction: How many fish do you see in this line? Tap to find out!
challenges.hint: Take your time and tap each fish as you say its number.
challenges.narration: Keep up the great counting! Let us count this line of fish.

challenges.instruction: Can you count this row of fish? Touch every one!
challenges.hint: Watch the running count as you tap each fish to keep track.
challenges.narration: Look at this longer line of fish. Let us count them all carefully.

challenges.instruction: Wonderful counting! Let us count even more fish in a line.
challenges.hint: Make sure you do not double-tap the same fish twice.
challenges.narration: We are getting higher! Let us count all seven fish together.

challenges.instruction: Can you count all the fish in this wonderful line?
challenges.hint: Tap slowly and check the number on each fish as you go.
challenges.narration: This is our biggest line yet. Let us count up to eight fish!

challenges.instruction: One more time! Count all the fish to show your skills.
challenges.hint: Touch each fish and listen to the counting song in your head.
challenges.narration: You are a counting star! Let us count these eight fish one final time.

judgement.reasoning: The student struggles with one-to-one correspondence and tracking (double counting / skipping). The detour uses the same activity engine, but drops the count down to 3, arranges items strictly in a line, enables highlight-on-tap and running counts, and gradually scales back up to 8.
judgement.verdict: Yes, starting with smaller sets arranged in a clean line with tap highlighting directly scaffolds tracking and one-to-one correspondence.
